title: Under the Hull to the Edge of AI: A Submariner’s Perspective on Joining One Stop Systems
summary: Eight years on fast-attack boats made my transition to the rugged edge computing environment feel entirely natural for three reasons: Designing systems to deliver information at speed, designing systems to operate in highly constrained environments, and serving the DoD with advanced computing projects.
body_text: By Patrick Millington, Product Manager When I recently hung up my NWUs after eight years in the U.S. Navy Submarine Force, I was navigating a unique transition balancing two very different but deeply intertwined identities: the operational reality of serving onboard fast-attack submarines, and the technical foundation of my Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) degree from Norwich University. I braced myself for the infamous "culture shock" of civilian corporate life. Transitioning from a world of hyper-disciplined, high-stakes undersea operations into the private sector is a path filled with uncertainty. You wonder if a niche operational skill set will translate, or if you’ll deeply miss the shared sense of critical mission focus. But walking into the headquarters of One Stop Systems (OSS) in Escondido, California, any lingering doubts instantly evaporated. As a new employee at OSS, it quickly became apparent that my years in the classroom at Norwich and my eight years under the hull were the perfect prologue for this role. While I’m no longer charting courses through dark ocean depths by listening (sonar), the fundamental mission remains exactly the same: ensuring that operators, whether they are down range or upstream at the innovating edge of computing, have access to the highest-performing, most reliable technology possible when failure is simply not an option. Eight years on fast-attack boats made my transition to the rugged edge computing environment feel entirely natural for three reasons: Designing systems to deliver information at speed, designing systems to operate in highly constrained environments, and serving the DoD with advanced computing projects. The High-Velocity World of Fast-Attacks Meets Edge AI On a fast-attack submarine (SSN), your mission is dynamic. Whether it's intelligence gathering, anti-submarine warfare, or strike operations, you are constantly collecting massive amounts of sensor and sonar data. You have to process that data, separate the signal from the noise, and make critical tactical decisions in real time. At OSS, I found a team obsessed with solving that exact data bottleneck. What OSS calls "AI Transportable" is the civilian equivalent of a fast-attack mission: packing datacenter-class compute power, lightning-fast PCIe architectures, the latest GPUs, and NVMe flash storage into ruggedized, compact footprints. Watching OSS design systems that ingest and process terabytes of sensor data at the edge felt like an advanced application of my degree at the speed demanded by SSNs. It’s the same processes I lead my teams through: processing data into information at the speed of relevancy. The Ultimate SWaP-C Challenge (Fast-Attack Style) Every submariner knows that space is the ultimate luxury, and on SSNs it is a luxury we cannot enjoy. We live and breathe SWaP-C (Size, Weight, Power, and Cost) constraints. If a system takes up too much room, generates unmanageable heat, or draws too much power from the grid, it doesn't make it past a drawing board, much less a hatch. OSS tackles this exact puzzle every day. Our team engineers liquid-immersion cooling systems for mobile tactical platforms and ruggedizes the Torrey 2U-SDSand 3U-SDS systems for extreme environments, bridging the gap between the tactical and academic. Speaking the Same Language Transitioning veterans often struggle to translate their tactical experience into corporate value. At OSS, that translation was instantaneous. When we discuss our defense projects, such as providing high-speed data recording and AI-enabled servers for Department of Defense platforms, I don't just see product numbers and tech specs. I see the faces of the junior sailors, sonar technicians, and tactical officers who will be relying on that system to maintain a combat advantage. OSS understands the defense ecosystem. From adhering to strict military environmental testing standards to building composable infrastructure that can adapt to changing mission parameters, the company builds with the operator in mind. Our mantra, "Performance Without Compromise," isn't just a marketing slogan; it’s an engineering mandate that echoes the absolute reliability demanded by the military to support their service members and dominate in every domain. Looking Ahead Joining One Stop Systems has allowed me to turn the page to an exciting new chapter without losing the sense of purpose that defined my eight years in the Navy. I’m no longer under the hull, but I am still proudly serving the mission. I am thrilled to be a part of the OSS team, working alongside brilliant minds to push the boundaries of what’s possible at the rugged edge.

title: Journey from automation to autonomy: How Pega Agentic AI is redefining enterprise operations
summary: Discover how agentic AI helps enterprises move beyond traditional automation to improve customer service, streamline operations, and deliver better outcomes.
body_text: Your customer just made a perfectly reasonable request in your customer service messenger. The problem is that it falls just outside your automated process. The system grinds to a halt. The answer is just disturbingly unhelpful. A support ticket is created, and the seamless experience you promised is broken. Sound familiar? This is the ceiling of traditional automation – a ceiling that is cracking under the weight of modern customer expectations. Enterprises today are at an inflection point. Customers are more demanding and tech-savvy than ever, expecting brands to be agile, flexible, and instantly responsive to their needs. This shift in customer expectation is forcing business leaders to ask a bigger question: How do we move beyond rigid, predefined processes to create an enterprise that can adapt on the fly? While traditional automation and decisioning were milestones in efficiency, they were not designed for this new reality. This is where agentic AI fundamentally changes the game. Agentic AI unlocks a transformative opportunity, infusing the enterprise with the power to handle both creative and analytical activities, and make your operations inherently more adaptable to changing customer needs and business strategies. And expectations are high! The World Economic Forum highlights that enterprises expect, on average, double-digit percentage increases in productivity and revenue growth within 18 months of deployment and scaling agentic AI, plus a similar reduction in costs. Why agentic AI matters now Across industries such as insurance, healthcare, and financial services, work has become more complex, regulated, and time-sensitive. A single customer interaction often spans multiple systems, roles, and decisions. Human workers spend disproportionate time gathering information, validating data, and coordinating next steps rather than applying judgment where it matters most. The idea of having systems that can reason, act, and collaborate with predictable precision is just the ultimate amplification of human ingenuity, freeing human minds from procedural tasks to focus on the strategic problems and human relations that we are uniquely suited to solve. By orchestrating intelligence across cases, data, knowledge, and automation, agent-based systems reduce cognitive load, shorten cycle times, and improve consistency , while keeping humans in control of critical decisions. Pega’s differentiated approach to agentic AI What makes Pega’s vision for Agentic AI so compelling is its deep integration with the core enterprise workflows. This approach stems from a fundamental understanding that businesses demand both the efficiency of automation and the unwavering consistency of a process with a primary focus on customer outcomes, regardless of whether a task is handled by a human or an AI agent . Unlike experimental copilots or bolted-on chat interfaces, Pega agents are embedded directly into the platform’s case management, decisioning, and automation fabric. This means that agents can: Drive consistent, predictable outcomes by operating natively within your established case types and process stages. Through Pega’s Center-out™ architecture , agents are anchored to the business logic, not to a chat interface. Enable smarter, secure, context-aware decisions by leveraging your existing enterprise data, knowledge repositories, and automation tools. Amplify team productivity by enabling seamless collaboration where agents handle procedural tasks, perform research, conduct initial analysis, and then pass work to human experts for critical judgments. Ensure enterprise-grade trust and safety by having every agent action automatically adhere to the same policy, compliance, and governance guardrails as your human team. Build with confidence on a trusted foundation by leveraging the power of a unified platform already recognized as a Leader in the G artner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Process Automation Technologies (BOAT) . Ultimately, this is what makes agentic AI with Pega practical, scalable, and production-ready – not just aspirational. What Aaseya’s participation in the Lighthouse Program means for clients Aaseya’s participation in the Pega Lighthouse Agentic Operations program represents a direct investment in helping clients move beyond experimentation and into production-grade, outcome-driven AI adoption of Pega’s agentic and Gen AI capabilities . As a Lighthouse partner, Aaseya has been working with Pega to industrialize real-world agentic solutions that operate on an enterprise scale. For clients, this translates into faster access to proven architectures, reusable accelerators, and implementation patterns that have been tested in complex, regulated environments. Aaseya starts with Pega Blueprint to co-design agentic workflows in real time, replacing months of requirements gathering with days of visual design. Organizations benefit from reusable components and solutions that already embed governance, explainability, security, and human-in-the-loop controls. Most importantly, Lighthouse participation ensures that Aaseya’s clients receive AI capabilities that are tightly aligned to business outcomes. Whether improving service responsiveness, reducing operational cost, or strengthening compliance, clients gain solutions that are designed to deliver measurable value from day one, while remaining adaptable as business needs evolve. The shift from old way to agentic way In a traditional claims or service environment, an adjuster often begins their day by logging into multiple disconnected systems. Policy data sits on one platform, medical records in another, claims history in a third, and correspondence in shared inboxes. To assemble a complete picture, the adjuster manually searches for documents, calls providers for missing information, and follows up with customers for clarifications. This fragmented process can take hours or even days. Decisions are delayed, errors are introduced through manual handling, and customers experience prolonged uncertainty and frustration. In an agentic environment powered by Pega, the process looks fundamentally different: Customers use the 24/7 available self-service to engage with the brand. Pega Conversation Agent smartly understands the context, asks/validates information, and initiates the right case. Pega’s Predictable AI™ Agents then seamlessly gather data from all relevant systems, request additional documents from customers, validate customer and policy information, analyze supporting documents, and apply business and medical rules in real time. Within seconds, the platform assembles a complete, verified case file. Potential risks or exceptions are flagged proactively, and recommended next actions are generated. The human adjuster receives a “ready-to-adjudicate” case, supported by transparent reasoning, supporting evidence, and recommendations. An assignment agent supports the adjuster by providing zero-hallucination access to case details, compliance guidelines and everything else needed to make the final decision. Instead of spending time on data collection, the adjuster focuses on judgment and decision-making. What previously took days is now completed in minutes, improving both operational efficiency and customer confidence. Pega + Aaseya: Leading the agentic transformation At Aaseya, we see agentic AI not as a layer of automation, but as a new operating model for enterprise work. Through the Lighthouse partnership, Aaseya is helping organizations design digital workforces where AI agents and human experts operate in coordinated, governed ecosystems. Want to learn more about our agentic architecture and how Aaseya and Pega are working together to build mission critical agentic operations? In a recent webinar, we dig into the 6Rs and provide real world examples of agentic operations at work, including a deep dive demo of agentic medical pre-authorization. Watch the webinar on demand today !

title: Grant Thornton Advisors Standardizes MSSP Operations on CrowdStrike Falcon Complete
summary: The advisory services leader consolidates its managed security operations on CrowdStrike, replacing legacy MDR with agentic MDR.
body_text: Leader in advisory services consolidates its managed security operations on CrowdStrike, combining human expertise with intelligent agents to stop breaches at machine speed for customers worldwide AUSTIN, Texas and CHICAGO – June 16, 2026 – CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (Grant Thornton Advisors) today announced that Grant Thornton Advisors is standardizing its managed security services on the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform , anchored by Falcon® Complete through the Falcon Complete for Service Providers program. Building on this strategy, Grant Thornton Advisors is expanding its global security managed services capabilities – further demonstrating the continued evolution of its multinational platform to serve clients operating across multiple jurisdictions. The move consolidates Grant Thornton Advisors’ managed security service provider (MSSP) capabilities around a unified operating model, enhancing the ability to deliver leading managed detection and response (MDR) solutions to customers worldwide through CrowdStrike’s Agentic MDR . Using intelligent agents to augment expert analysts, Agentic MDR automates high-friction workflows and scales elite managed protection across enterprise environments to stop AI-accelerated adversaries moving at machine speed. The partnership underscores Grant Thornton Advisors’ continued investment in delivering measurable security outcomes for clients across industries and geographies in key markets around the globe. "Our clients don't need more tools – they need security that actually works," said Tony Buffomante, national managing partner of cyber and risk services at Grant Thornton Advisors LLC. "With Falcon Complete at the core of our managed security operations, we're pairing CrowdStrike's detection and response capabilities with our advisory, incident response, and managed engineering expertise to help clients move from reactive security postures to proactive, measurable protection wherever our clients are located. That's what outcome-driven security looks like – and it's what our clients are asking for." In this approach, Grant Thornton Advisors is bringing a new portfolio of managed security services to market, including tiered MDR offerings and managed engineering services. These services layer proactive threat hunting, automated response, and platform optimization on top of Falcon Complete – giving customers more insights from their own telemetry data that leads to a single, integrated path to a stronger security posture and reduced risk. This signals a broader shift in the MDR market as advisory firms move away from legacy MDR and fragmented security operations toward the unified Falcon platform. The announcement comes amid an aggressive growth period for Grant Thornton Advisors, which has expanded its advisory capabilities through a series of acquisitions – including Auxis, Stax, and the recently-announced agreement to acquire MCA Connect – while building a multinational platform that now spans nearly 20 markets with almost 25,000 professionals. “Organizations are done stitching together point solutions that simply cannot deliver desired results,” said Daniel Bernard, chief business officer at CrowdStrike. “The next generation of MDR is moving from tools to services that actually execute. Grant Thornton Advisors’ choice to standardize on Falcon Complete is about bringing a new class of managed security services to market – combining our Agentic MDR with their advisory, engineering, and operational expertise to deliver security outcomes at scale. This is where the market is going.” To learn more about Grant Thornton Advisors’ managed security services built on the CrowdStrike Falcon platform, visit: grantthornton.com . About CrowdStrike CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD), a global cybersecurity leader, has redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced cloud-native platform for protecting critical areas of enterprise risk – endpoints and cloud workloads, identity and data. Powered by the CrowdStrike Security Cloud and world-class AI, the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform leverages real-time indicators of attack, threat intelligence, evolving adversary tradecraft, and enriched telemetry from across the enterprise to deliver hyper-accurate detections, automated protection and remediation, elite threat hunting, and prioritized observability of vulnerabilities. Purpose-built in the cloud with a single lightweight-agent architecture, the Falcon platform delivers rapid and scalable deployment, superior protection and performance, reduced complexity, and immediate time-to-value. CrowdStrike owns other trademarks and service marks and may use the brands of third parties to identify their products and services. About the Grant Thornton Advisors multinational platform The Grant Thornton Advisors multinational platform is a group of firms within the Grant Thornton International Limited network that connects priority markets and operates with aligned standards, technology and delivery expectations. Firms remain locally led and legally separate. The Grant Thornton International Limited network provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets. The platform is currently home to almost 20 aligned firms stretching from the Americas across Europe and the Middle East to the Asia-Pacific region. These firms bring together almost 25,000 professionals to deliver cross-border solutions powered by advanced technologies, a shared commitment to quality and a growing reputation as the industry’s employer-of-choice. title: Retool alternatives: how to pick the right internal app builder in 2026
summary: Many teams that adopted Retool between 2017 and 2024 are now re-evaluating their stack. Retool's per user pricing, tighter restrictions on self hosting, and governance feature gating have pushed buyers to seriously compare retool alternatives against a consistent set of criteria. This guide cuts through the marketing noise and focuses
body_text: Many teams that adopted Retool between 2017 and 2024 are now re-evaluating their stack. Retool's per user pricing, tighter restrictions on self hosting, and governance feature gating have pushed buyers to seriously compare retool alternatives against a consistent set of criteria. This guide cuts through the marketing noise and focuses on practical selection factors - build speed, data connectivity, deployment, security, and total cost - so you can match the right platform to your actual constraints. Key Takeaways The best retool alternatives depend on your team's technical skills, data security requirements, deployment model (cloud vs. self-hosted vs. air-gapped), and whether you're building purely internal tools or also shipping client portals and mobile apps. Evaluate every Retool competitor across a consistent framework: build speed, integrations with multiple data sources, extensibility through custom code and custom components, authentication and permissions, deployment flexibility, governance, and total cost of ownership. Tools like Jet Admin, Appsmith, Superblocks, Microsoft Power Apps, ToolJet, Budibase, Bubble, Glide, and Softr each occupy different "best for" niches. There is no single universal winner. This article includes a scannable comparison table, per-tool "best for / strengths / limitations" breakdowns, and a practical migration checklist for teams moving away from Retool. Why teams are looking for Retool alternatives in 2026 Retool is a low code platform for building internal tools, admin panels, and dashboards on top of existing databases and APIs. It became popular because of its rich component library, deep SQL and JavaScript support, and ability to let engineering teams ship internal apps in hours instead of weeks. Retool supports extensive database integrations for internal tools and remains a strong product. Retool is classified as a low-code platform, not no-code - meaning Retool is not a true no-code platform, and non technical users typically need developer support. So why the search for alternatives? Several friction points have intensified: Pricing pressure. Retool starts at $10/month per builder, but costs escalate quickly with large internal user bases and external users. Retool's per user pricing becomes painful when you're rolling tools out to hundreds or thousands of end users. Deployment constraints. Retool can be self-hosted but requires significant DevOps resources, and self-hosted deployment is now gated behind Enterprise plans , making it less accessible for smaller teams or those needing on premise deployment without enterprise contracts. Vendor lock-in. All UI layouts, queries, and logic live inside Retool's proprietary builder. If you ever need to leave, there's no clean way to export an app's source code. Limited client-facing and mobile support. Retool excels at internal dashboards, but teams wanting polished client portals, native mobile apps, or progressive web apps often hit design and branding limits. Recent additions like Retool Assist and AI Agents improve app generation speed, but they don't address code portability or long-term platform dependence. Consider a 30-person ops team rolling tools out to 1,000+ internal users, a fintech requiring strict on-prem, or a SaaS company wanting to ship client portals - each has different reasons to look beyond Retool. This article will not argue that Retool is "bad." Instead, it will help you match the right alternative to your specific constraints and internal tooling roadmap. How to evaluate Retool alternatives: the 8-part framework Before comparing specific tools, your team should agree on evaluation criteria. This prevents choosing a platform purely based on a pricing page or a polished demo. Pricing structures can vary significantly between low-code platforms, so a framework keeps comparisons honest. Here are the eight dimensions that matter most: Build speed and UX. Look for a visual builder with a drag and drop interface, pre built components, templates for common internal tools, and AI assistance that can generate apps from natural language prompts. Good tools get you to a working prototype in hours, not days. Data connectivity. Native connectors to databases, REST API endpoints, GraphQL, SaaS apps, and Google Sheets. The platform supports joining multiple data sources in one app without brittle workarounds. Extensibility and custom code. Support for both javascript and Python, TypeScript, serverless functions, and custom components (React, Vue). You should be able to add custom javascript or write custom logic without leaving the platform. Low-code platforms require some coding knowledge for advanced features, while no-code platforms require no programming skills to use. Authentication and permissions. Single sign on (SSO/SAML), SCIM provisioning, role based access control, granular access controls, and row-level security. Support for external users directories is critical for client portals. Deployment model. Fully managed cloud, self-hosted on your own infrastructure, hybrid, and air-gapped options. Self-hosting is a popular choice for teams prioritizing data privacy. Evaluate how updates and patches are handled. Governance and operations. Staging environments, approval workflows, audit logs, git sync and Git-based version control, CI/CD pipelines, and change management. These matter more than most teams realize - especially under compliance pressure. Pricing model and scalability. Per-builder vs. per end user pricing, feature-gated tiers, and what happens when you scale to thousands of internal users or unlimited end users. Watch for hidden overage costs. Maintenance and long-term risk. Vendor lock in risk, ability to export or recreate apps, ecosystem maturity, documentation quality, and support SLAs. Open-source platforms often provide greater control over data and customization, but add maintenance overhead. Turn these criteria into an internal checklist or RFP matrix before demoing any platform. Quick comparison: top Retool alternatives at a glance This section gives you a skimmable overview. Deeper per-tool breakdowns follow in the next sections. Low-code platforms typically streamline the development of internal business tools, but each tool below occupies a different niche. Platform Best for App types Data connectivity Deployment Extensibility Pricing approach Jet Admin Secure business apps on existing data Internal tools, client portals, dashboards, web apps SQL/NoSQL, REST APIs, SaaS, spreadsheets Cloud, self-hosted Custom JS, generated logic Per plan with generous external user allotments Superblocks Governed enterprise internal tools Internal apps, workflows, automations SQL/NoSQL, REST APIs, SaaS Cloud, hybrid (on-prem agents) JS, Python, clean react code, custom components ~$49/user/mo (paid plans) Appsmith Open-source internal apps for dev teams Internal tools, dashboards, admin panels SQL/NoSQL, REST, GraphQL Cloud, self-hosted, air-gapped (enterprise) JS, custom widgets Free self-hosted; paid from $15/user/mo ToolJet Flexible open-source with Python support Internal apps, dashboards 75+ data sources, SQL, REST, GraphQL Cloud, on-prem JS, Python Free tier; enterprise plans for governance Budibase Self-hostable CRUD apps and workflow automation Admin panels, internal tools, custom apps MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, REST APIs Cloud, self-hosted (all plans) JS scripting, plugins Free for ≤5 users; paid from ~$19/mo Microsoft Power Apps Microsoft-centric enterprises Canvas/model-driven apps, mobile apps SharePoint, Dynamics 365, Dataverse, 400+ connectors Microsoft Cloud Power Fx, custom connectors ~$12/user/mo at scale Bubble Complex customer-facing web apps SaaS apps, marketplaces, full apps REST APIs, plugins Bubble cloud Visual logic, plugins Free tier; paid plans scale by usage Glide Spreadsheet-to-app for small teams Mobile apps, simple internal tools Google Sheets, Airtable, Excel Cloud Limited custom code Free version; paid per app Softr No-code client portals Client portals, directories, web apps Airtable, Google Sheets, databases Cloud No-code blocks Free tier; paid per site UI Bakery Internal dashboards with AI generation Admin panels, dashboards SQL/NoSQL, APIs Cloud, on-prem JS, SQL Per builder Patterns to notice: Appsmith, ToolJet, and Budibase form an open-source cohort where using open-source tools can mitigate concerns of vendor lock-in. Power Apps dominates when Microsoft tools are already everywhere. Jet Admin and Softr stand out for client portals and external users. Superblocks targets enterprises needing governance and high-performance platforms generally more suitable for handling large datasets. Jet Admin: best for secure business apps on existing data Jet Admin is a platform for building secure business apps and internal tools on top of existing data sources. It can generate the interface and application/backend logic, then deploy apps to internal users or external users - making it a strong fit for both internal tools and client portals. Best for: Teams that want to create apps and business portals on existing databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools, with AI-assisted UI and logic generation. Strengths: Broad connector catalog spanning relational databases, REST APIs, spreadsheets (including Google Sheets), and popular SaaS systems. Consult the Jet Admin integrations page for the current supported list. Ability to generate app UIs and multi step workflows directly from existing schemas, reducing time to deploy apps significantly. Support for workflow automation, approval flows, and CRUD app generation without writing everything from scratch. Options suited for SMB through enterprise, with enterprise security features, SSO, audit logs, and granular access controls available on higher tiers. Competitive external user pricing - Jet Admin offers generous external user seat allotments at fixed cost, compared to Retool's per-seat charges that add up quickly. Limitations: Jet Admin's visual builder is powerful for most custom internal tools, but teams requiring very low-level nested JSON manipulation or deeply custom React-like frontends may find less raw JavaScript intensity compared to developer-first platforms like Retool or Appsmith. Jet Admin works as an ai app builder that can generate apps - including admin panels, approval workflows, or client portals - from existing data models, while still allowing manual refinements. Shortlist Jet Admin over Retool when you want to stay close to your existing business data, prioritize secure deployments, and value a code platform that generates both UI and backend logic rather than only UI layers. Learn more in the Jet Admin vs Retool comparison and explore Jet Admin's app-building capabilities . Superblocks: hybrid enterprise platform with clean code output Superblocks is an internal developer platform oriented toward enterprises that want AI-assisted internal tools, automations, and workflows. It targets engineering-heavy teams that value code quality and governance alongside visual building. Superblocks provides AI-native app generation with no vendor lock-in, and the platform supports exporting clean react code so teams aren't trapped. Best for: Large or regulated enterprises with strong engineering teams wanting a mix of visual building, AI-generated flows, and readable code output. Strengths: Superblocks provides a hybrid deployment model for self-hosting using on-prem agents, keeping data within your network while the control plane stays managed. Enterprise governance and CI/CD are important features for platforms like Superblocks - it delivers environment separation, approval workflows, audit logs, and version control. Security and governance are key considerations for enterprise platforms like Superblocks, with SSO, RBAC, and network isolation via agents. Superblocks is ideal for enterprises needing high-performance applications with complex multi step workflows. Limitations: There's a steep learning curve for non-developers. Pricing (~$49/user/mo for enterprise plans) and the enterprise focus may be overkill for small teams or simple internal apps. Compared to Retool, Superblocks emphasizes code portability and hybrid deployment more aggressively. Compared to Jet Admin, Superblocks is a stronger fit when engineering teams want close-to-code control, while Jet Admin suits teams preferring a higher-level app builder that can generate UI and logic directly from data models. Appsmith: open-source internal tools for developer-led teams Appsmith is a well-known open-source alternative to Retool, focused on low-code UI building, JavaScript-based logic, and broad adoption among developer-led teams building internal tools and dashboards. Effective alternatives to Retool include open-source options for self-hosting, and Appsmith leads that category. Best for: Engineering or data teams who prefer open source, self-hosting, and a JavaScript-centric app builder for internal tools. Strengths: Appsmith supports self-hosting with no per-user fees - the free community edition lets you run unlimited apps on your own infrastructure with no user limits. Strong git sync support and Git-based version control for managing changes across environments. Ability to connect to SQL/NoSQL databases, REST, and GraphQL using custom javascript and a visual query builder. Appsmith's paid plans start at $15/month per user , with enterprise tiers adding SAML/OIDC/SCIM, air-gapped deployment, and managed hosting. Limitations: Self-hosting adds DevOps overhead for patching, backups, and monitoring. Fewer AI-native features than newer commercial competitors. Non technical users unfamiliar with JavaScript face a learning curve. Compared to Retool and Jet Admin, Appsmith offers similar drag-and-drop components and a query builder, but trades ease-of-use for openness and infrastructure control. Appsmith offers a free self-hosted edition with no per-user fees, making it the strongest choice when a company already has in-house developer capacity and values full control over source code. ToolJet and Budibase: flexible open-source internal app builders ToolJet and Budibase are frequently evaluated together by teams seeking open-source retool alternatives with strong visual builders and workflow automation for building internal tools. ToolJet Best for: Developer-friendly low-code internal apps with flexibility and both cloud and on-prem hosting options. Strengths: ToolJet connects to over 75 data sources for flexibility, including APIs and databases. ToolJet supports SQL, REST, and GraphQL for database interaction. ToolJet is praised for its flexibility and Python support, alongside JavaScript - enabling both javascript and Python in custom logic. ToolJet supports both cloud-based and on-prem hosting options, giving teams control over deployment. Enterprise features like SSO and audit logs available on higher tiers. Limitations: AI and advanced governance features may be gated to paid editions. The free tier can restrict builder counts. Complexity rises as apps scale. Budibase Best for: Teams wanting a low code platform for CRUD-style internal apps, admin panels, and workflow-heavy tools. Strengths: Budibase is an open-source platform for building internal tools with a built-in database plus external connectors. Budibase connects to MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and REST APIs. Budibase offers a drag-and-drop frontend builder for app creation, and emphasizes rapid creation of CRUD applications and workflow automation. Budibase is free for up to 5 users on the cloud , and Budibase allows self-hosting on all plans, even free. Role based access control and decent self-hosting support out of the box. Limitations: May feel constrained for highly custom UIs or complex business logic. Cloud AI features and higher user limits are typically reserved for paid plans. Both tools are more open and self-hosting-friendly than Retool's standard cloud, and more DIY than Jet Admin's generated interface and logic approach. While open source reduces license costs, factor in the overhead of managing upgrades, security patches, backups, and monitoring on your own infrastructure. Microsoft Power Apps: best Retool alternative for Microsoft-centric enterprises Microsoft Power Apps is part of the broader Microsoft Power Platform , and its deep integration with Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, and Power BI makes it a natural retool alternative for organizations already standardized on microsoft tools. Best for: Large organizations heavily invested in Microsoft cloud, needing low-code apps and internal tools tied closely to SharePoint, Dataverse, and Teams. Strengths: Microsoft Power Apps integrates deeply with SharePoint and Dynamics 365, plus hundreds of additional connectors within the Microsoft ecosystem. Canvas and model-driven apps with native mobile app support through the Power Apps mobile client, enabling teams to build and deploy apps across desktop and android apps. Extensive governance: environment separation, DLP policies, admin controls via the CoE toolkit, and identity management through Azure AD. Power Apps costs $12/month/user at 2,000+ users, which can be cost-effective for large enterprises already paying for Microsoft 365 licensing. Limitations: Power Apps can be intimidating for new users initially due to its formula language (Power Fx) and layered configuration. Connecting many third-party, non-Microsoft data sources can add complexity and licensing cost. Non-Microsoft shops may find it limiting, and the app's source code isn't portable outside the Power Platform. Power apps is generally not the first choice for teams wanting portable, framework-agnostic code, but is extremely compelling where Microsoft is already the core platform for identity, data, and collaboration. Bubble, Glide, and Softr: no-code frontends and client portals Not all retool alternatives focus solely on internal tools. Bubble, Glide, and Softr lean toward no-code web apps, client portals, and customer-facing experiences. No-code tools allow users to build apps without technical expertise, which matters for teams without dedicated engineers. Bubble Best for: Complex customer-facing web apps and full apps built with no-code, where teams are comfortable adopting the Bubble runtime. Strengths: Highly flexible visual editor, plugin ecosystem, support for marketplaces and SaaS-style apps, and richer UX than typical internal tools builders. Limitations: Steeper learning curve than simpler no code tools. Apps are reliant on Bubble's hosting and runtime. Code is not exportable in a traditional full-code sense. Glide Best for: Quickly turning spreadsheets (Google Sheets, Excel, Airtable) into internal mobile apps and web apps for small to mid-sized teams. Strengths: Excellent mobile-first UX and spreadsheet-native mindset. Very approachable for non technical users and field teams needing native mobile apps or progressive web apps. Limitations: More constrained UI and logic compared to developer-oriented low-code tools. Better suited to simple internal tools and directories than deeply custom workflows. Softr Best for: Client portals and simple internal tools built on top of business data in Airtable, Google Sheets, or other connected data sources. Softr is a no-code builder for creating apps from existing databases. Strengths: Block-based builder - Softr uses a simple drag-and-drop editor for app creation. Rich library of portal patterns. Quick to stand up secure client or partner experiences. Limitations: Less suited to complex multi-step automations or intricate backend logic. Design and component gating can frustrate advanced users. Collectively, these three are more opinionated about data sources and stronger where UX and client-facing experiences matter more than deep internal workflow logic. Compared to Jet Admin, they trade backend power for frontend polish and speed for non technical users. Also worth noting: Blaze allows unlimited app creation without coding skills and Blaze offers no-code simplicity for building unlimited apps, while Noloco caters to non-technical users for creating applications quickly - both serve similar audiences. Other notable Retool competitors in 2026 The retool alternatives landscape is large. Here are a few additional credible tools you'll encounter in 2026 evaluations. UI Bakery Best for: Internal tools, admin panels, and dashboards with a strong focus on responsive UI control. UI Bakery provides capabilities for generating applications with AI assistance, helping teams scaffold custom apps faster. Strengths: Low-code visual builder with SQL/NoSQL and API support; collaboration and Git integration; on-prem or cloud deployment options. Limitations: Primarily focused on internal business apps. No straightforward code export. Xano Best for: No-code/low-code backend APIs, logic, and databases that can power frontends built in other tools. Strengths: Scalable PostgreSQL-based backend, API-first, logic flows for complex business rules. Good pairing with frontend app builders like Jet Admin, Bubble, or custom React. Limitations: Not an internal UI builder by itself - needs a separate app builder for frontends. Gumloop Gumloop is a no-code platform for building internal tools and building apps instantly. Gumloop allows app creation using plain language prompts - users can build apps in plain language without writing code. Gumloop allows integration with Google Calendar and Slack for automation, and Gumloop uses credits for actual usage, not per-user fees. It's early-stage but notable for teams exploring natural language-driven development. AI-native internal-tools platforms and workflow orchestrators are emerging rapidly in 2025–2026, with a focus on agents and LLM orchestration. While promising, many are still maturing in governance and production-readiness compared to established tools. Map any new platform back to the 8-part evaluation framework before committing. Comparing Jet Admin vs Retool vs open-source builders Buyers often narrow down to one platform from each of three buckets: Retool, Jet Admin, and the open-source cohort (Appsmith, ToolJet, Budibase). Here's how they compare across key dimensions: Ownership and openness. Retool and Jet Admin are proprietary, managed platforms. Appsmith, ToolJet, and Budibase offer open-source cores with visible source and self-hosting options. Open-source platforms often provide greater control over data and customization, but shift operational burden to your team. Data connectivity. All support multiple data sources - SQL/NoSQL databases, REST APIs, and more. Jet Admin and Retool add curated SaaS connectors. Open-source tools often rely on community connectors and custom integrations. Governance and security. Retool and Jet Admin provide enterprise-ready data security and governance (SSO, audit logs, granular permissions) per their documentation. Open-source tools provide many controls but rely on the buyer's own infra hardening and update discipline. Build experience. Jet Admin and Retool emphasize visual builders and templates. Jet Admin adds generated UI and logic from existing data. Open-source tools lean on developers familiar with JavaScript or similar, with pre built components that are functional but less polished. When each approach tends to win: Jet Admin or Retool: when teams want fast time-to-value, strong guardrails, and fully managed infrastructure. Open source: when infrastructure control and license cost reduction matter more than turnkey convenience. Jet Admin vs Retool specifically: Jet Admin offers more generous external user allotments at fixed pricing versus Retool's per-seat model, and can generate both UI and backend workflows from existing schemas. Pilot at least one platform from each category before making a long-term decision. Choosing the best Retool alternative for your team type The best retool alternatives are context-dependent. Here's how to translate the earlier comparisons into concrete recommendations by team profile: Small, non-technical operations teams needing simple internal tools fast: lean toward no code platforms like Glide, Softr, or a higher-level builder like Jet Admin that can generate interfaces quickly. No-code platforms require no programming skills to use, which keeps adoption fast. Mid-sized SaaS or startup teams with a few engineers owning internal apps: consider Jet Admin, Appsmith, or ToolJet depending on your appetite for self-hosting vs. managed cloud and how much custom code you want to write. A free plan or free tier lets you validate before committing. Large enterprises with strong IT and security functions: shortlist Superblocks, Power Apps, Jet Admin, and possibly open-source platforms with self-hosting, depending on regulatory requirements and Microsoft adoption. Enterprise pricing and enterprise plans should include SSO, audit logs, and on premise deployment. Agencies or B2B companies shipping client portals: focus on Jet Admin, Softr, Bubble, or similar tools with stronger client-facing UI capabilities and robust authentication for external users. Teams prioritizing AI-native workflows: consider platforms emphasizing natural language prompts and AI generation, while checking governance maturity. An ai app builder can dramatically cut time to first version, but production apps still benefit from developer oversight. Weight data security, governance, and app criticality more heavily when internal tools touch PII, finance, healthcare, or regulated workloads. The upcoming migration and governance sections can be turned into an internal decision document. Migration checklist: moving from Retool to an alternative Switching internal-tool platforms is less about code and more about planning: inventorying apps, data sources, and stakeholders. Inventory and categorize existing Retool apps. Group by criticality (mission-critical vs. convenience), by department (ops, support, finance), and by complexity (CRUD-only vs. heavy custom logic and JS). Identify which are unlimited apps and which have per end user pricing implications. Map data sources and auth patterns. Document which databases, APIs, and third-party SaaS tools each app touches. Record user groups, roles, SSO setups, and any row-level security rules. Choose target platforms per app type. Simple CRUD dashboards might move to Jet Admin or Budibase. Complex React-like frontends might migrate to Superblocks or custom code backed by Xano. Admin panels with workflow automation could go to ToolJet or Appsmith. Run one to two pilot migrations. Pick medium-complexity apps, rebuild them in the target platform, and validate performance, usability, and security with real internal users. Use this to benchmark build speed and data connectivity. Plan coexistence and cutover. Operate Retool and the new platform side-by-side for a defined window. Ensure links, bookmarks, and permissions are updated. Communicate timelines to stakeholders clearly. Decommission and archive. Once traffic has shifted, archive Retool apps, revoke credentials, and ensure data retention and compliance obligations are met. AI-enabled builders - including Jet Admin - can reduce rebuild time by generating UIs and logic from existing schemas or plain language app descriptions. Create internal runbooks for each migration phase. Governance, data security, and compliance considerations For many organizations - especially in finance, healthcare, or B2B SaaS - governance and data security matter more than the visual builder experience when choosing a retool alternative. Key governance dimensions to review with each vendor: Authentication and authorization. Single sign on via SAML, OAuth, SCIM provisioning, just-in-time provisioning, granular roles, and row-level security where needed. Role based access control should extend to external users and internal users alike. Data residency and deployment. Cloud regions, VPC peering, private cloud or self-hosted options, air-gapped deployments, and how data traverses between the app builder and your data sources. On premise deployment matters for regulated industries. Auditability. Detailed audit logs of user actions, changes to apps, and production incidents. Integration with SIEM tools where available. Version control through git sync supports change tracking. Change management. Staging environments, approvals, Git integration, CI/CD, and the ability to roll back deployments safely. Open-source platforms shift some security responsibility onto internal teams. While they can be deployed in tightly controlled environments, patching, hardening, and monitoring become in-house tasks. Jet Admin invests in enterprise-grade security and governance - including SSO, audit logs, granular access controls, and deployment options suited for data-sensitive environments. Verify exact certifications, controls, and deployment models directly from the current Jet Admin documentation before making commitments. Security, DevOps, and data teams should participate early in any Retool replacement project. Proof-of-concept deployments should include security reviews, not just feature demos. Conclusion: narrowing down your list of Retool alternatives There is no single "best Retool alternative." Instead, there are clusters of tools optimized for internal tools, open-source control, Microsoft ecosystems, client portals, or AI-native workflows. The right choice depends on your team's skills, deployment requirements, and whether you're building custom internal tools, client portals, or mobile apps. Use the 8-part evaluation framework - build speed, data connectivity, extensibility, auth and permissions, deployment, governance, pricing model, and maintenance - and turn it into a concrete comparison sheet across your top three to five candidates. Example shortlists for common situations: "We're a scale-up with 5–10 engineers and many internal users" → evaluate Jet Admin, Retool, Appsmith, and ToolJet. "We're an enterprise with Microsoft 365 everywhere" → compare Power Apps, Jet Admin, Superblocks, and possibly open-source if self-hosting is mandatory. "We need polished client portals on top of existing data" → look at Jet Admin, Softr, Bubble. If you're ready to test your shortlist, consider trialing Jet Admin alongside at least one other contender. Benchmark build speed, data connectivity, and governance in your own environment with your real data sources. That's the only way to know which platform actually fits. FAQ about Retool alternatives These FAQs cover questions not fully explored in the main sections. What is the best Retool alternative for non-technical teams? Non-technical or lightly technical teams usually prefer true no code tools such as Glide, Softr, or a higher-level app builder like Jet Admin, which can generate much of the UI and custom logic from existing data and simple configuration instead of JavaScript. These platforms let non technical users ship working web apps and internal tools without writing code. Can I replace Retool with open-source tools without increasing risk? Open-source platforms like Appsmith, ToolJet, and Budibase can absolutely replace Retool in many scenarios. However, risk shifts from vendor to internal teams - they must handle hosting, backups, security patches, and monitoring. Appsmith offers a free self-hosted edition with no user limits, which keeps license costs at zero, but operational overhead is real. For some organizations this trade-off is acceptable; for others a managed no code platform with strong SLAs is safer. How important is native mobile support when choosing a Retool alternative? Importance depends on where users work. If most usage is desktop-based (ops, finance, back-office), browser-first tools like Retool or Jet Admin are often enough. If teams are in the field or on the go, platforms like Glide, Power Apps, or others with native mobile apps and native mobile app support can materially improve adoption. Do AI-native builders fully remove the need for developers? AI-native builders and assistants can dramatically cut time-to-first-version by generating internal apps and workflows from natural language prompts. But production-grade tools still benefit from developer oversight for security, data modeling, performance, and integration edge cases. Treat AI generation as a starting point, not the finish line. How long does it typically take to migrate off Retool? Timelines vary by app count and complexity. Small teams replacing a handful of dashboards may migrate in weeks, while large enterprises with dozens of mission-critical internal tools should plan for a phased migration over several months - including pilots, coexistence with the team plan on both platforms, and formal cutover windows.

title: Building a mature AI ecosystem for scalable impact
summary: As organizations continue to explore and adopt advanced forms of artificial intelligence (AI), one theme consistently emerges; success doesn’t come from any one tool, technology, or quick win.
body_text: As organizations continue to explore and adopt advanced forms of artificial intelligence (AI), one theme consistently emerges; success doesn’t come from any one tool, technology, or quick win. We see this play out through our own AI adoption within CGI, our work with clients, and our annual Voice of Our Clients (VOC) research. For example, VOC data shows organizations that adopt an ecosystem mindset , viewing AI not as a single technology but as an integrated network of capabilities, enablers, and policies, are not only more mature in their AI capabilities, but also achieve more meaningful outcomes. Many organizations begin their AI journey with individual tools or use cases. These early efforts are important, but they often remain isolated. Insights from VOC data reveal that a strategic ecosystem approach accelerates AI implementation maturity. For example: Digital leaders are ahead in GenAI implementation, with 32% in progress or having implemented GenAI versus 19% who are building or launching their digital strategies. Organizations with a holistic AI strategy have 6.6x higher maturity* in GenAI. Cloud adopters experience up to 1.9x greater GenAI maturity* than those that do not use cloud-based solutions to store data. A holistic data strategy results in a 5x increase in GenAI maturity.* * Higher maturity represents those executives who responded that they are in progress or have completed implementing GenAI initiatives. In simple terms, the right strategic approach increases positive impact. It’s not about doing more; it’s about doing it right, with purpose and alignment. Why ecosystem thinking matters Rather than focusing on single-point solutions, mature organizations take an ecosystem approach , integrating data, governance, infrastructure, talent, and security in support of their mission or business priorities. This approach rests on six interconnected pillars: High-quality data Data fuels every AI decision. Without trusted, timely, and interoperable data, even the most powerful models fall short. Talent AI should enhance people, not replace them. Organizations that invest in training, new roles, and change leadership are better prepared to sustain transformation. Mission-aligned infrastructure Scalable, secure infrastructure—whether on-premises, cloud, or hybrid—ensures AI systems are resilient and able to support evolving use cases, including agentic AI. Governance by design Responsible AI requires clear frameworks for ethics, transparency, and accountability—not as a bolt-on, but as part of the initial design, ongoing governance, and operational tools in place. Strategic alignment The most mature organizations are those that align AI with measurable business and mission outcomes, avoiding innovation theater and focusing on what matters most. Security embedded at every layer As AI systems grow in complexity and autonomy, so must the security frameworks that support them—from cyber resilience to continuous monitoring. Scaling at the right pace Not every organization needs to become an AI leader overnight. What matters most is intentional progress connected to overall organizational strategy and clear business outcomes. For organizations early in their journey, proven, repeatable solutions with clear business outcomes can build confidence. We have helped clients achieve tangible business outcomes using AI (visit our AI client success stories ). For more advanced clients, exploring new use cases and co-designing integrated solutions becomes the next frontier. In either case, the key is to treat AI adoption as a journey, not a destination. Looking ahead: Partnering with purpose AI continues to evolve, offering new possibilities for economic, social, and operational transformation. But, as we’ve learned through thousands of client engagements, sustainable impact isn’t about chasing what’s new—it’s about aligning what’s essential . The organizations that succeed will: Understand where they are on the maturity curve Take a whole-system view of their AI investments Commit to building capabilities that reinforce one another over time At CGI, we work alongside our clients to co-create AI ecosystems that are grounded in strategy, shaped by human needs, and designed to scale responsibly. Whether you’re just starting or ready to deepen your maturity, we’re here to help you navigate the journey, with insights you can act on. For further discussion on this topic, contact one of us for a conversation. Also, learn more about CGI’s AI work and capabilities .
